profile.summary: DNAGPT is a GPT-style DNA language model from Tencent AI Lab and collaborators. It reads a DNA sequence, split into 6-letter words, and can also take numbers as input; it can generate new DNA sequence, classify a sequence or predict a numerical value such as mRNA expression level. Pre-training adds two side tasks, predicting whether a sequence was reversed and predicting its GC content, to the usual next-token prediction.
profile.summary_source_locator: arXiv v3: author affiliations; arXiv abstract; README.md: Test examples; test.py get_model

summary_quotes.text: By enhancing the classic GPT model with a binary classification task (DNA sequence order), a numerical regression task (guanine-cytosine content prediction), and a comprehensive token language, DNAGPT can handle versatile DNA analysis tasks while processing both sequence and numerical data.
Human RNA experssion level regression model

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: DNAGPT is a decoder-only Transformer: the 0.1B model has 12 blocks of unidirectional attention, 12 heads each and a hidden size of 768. The DNA sequence is cut into non-overlapping k-mers, and numbers are encoded as separate number tokens; each token type has its own embedding layer and output head. Pre-training combines three tasks: next-token prediction, GC-content prediction for a random segment, and prediction of whether the sequence order was flipped. Reversing sequences lets the left-to-right model use context from both directions. For a downstream task the needed heads are kept and the model is fine-tuned.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The paper describes four pre-trained variants: DNAGPT-H (0.1 billion parameters, human reference genome, 4096 tokens), DNAGPT-M (0.1 billion, reference genomes of 9 species, 4096 tokens), DNAGPT-S-512 (0.1 billion, all mammalian reference genomes, 512 tokens) and DNAGPT-B-512 (3 billion, all mammalian reference genomes, 512 tokens). The repository releases three foundation checkpoints, dna_gpt0.1b_h, dna_gpt0.1b_m and dna_gpt3b_m, plus two fine-tuned checkpoints: an expression-level regression model and an AATAAA genomic signal classification model. The README calls the 3B checkpoint multi-organism and does not map file names to the paper's variant names. A result should name the checkpoint file.

DNAGPT-H, DNAGPT-M and DNAGPT-S-512 have 0.1 billion parameters and DNAGPT-B-512 has 3 billion parameters.

DNAGPT-H’s sequence length is set to 4096, equivalent to 24,576 bps, and its pre-training data is based on Human reference genomes; DNAGPT-M also has a sequence length of 4096, with pre-training data from reference genomes of 9 species; DNAGPT-S-512 and DNAGPT-B-512 have a sequence length set to 512 and its pre-training data consists of reference genomes from all mammals.

facts.label: Training data

DNAGPT-S-512 and DNAGPT-B-512: all mammalian reference genomes from NCBI GenBank, about 200 billion bps sampled after preprocessing. Sequences with an N content ratio greater than 0.05 were removed.

run_guide.summary: Get the DNAGPT code, place the human 0.1B checkpoint in the checkpoints folder and generate ten DNA sequences from a short prompt.
prerequisites: PyTorch 2.0.0 or later and numpy, from requirements.txt.
The checkpoint dna_gpt0.1b_h.pth, downloaded by hand from the Google Drive or Tencent Weiyun links in the README.
A GPU is used when available; the README does not state hardware needs.
The code is under the PolyForm Noncommercial licence 1.0.0.
